# Initialisation
We invoke the key modules which we will use.
```{julia}
using Compose, Colors, Measures

import EpidemicsCFTP
epi = EpidemicsCFTP
```

A brief summary description of the `julia` package `Compose.jl` 
(the key package for producing these graphics)
can be found at 
<https://giovineitalia.github.io/Compose.jl/latest/gallery/forms/>.

Basic simulation parameters are the `population` size 
and the `duration` (assumes epidemic simulation commences at time `0`).
```{julia}
const popn     = 5 ;
const duration = 2 ;

const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if popn > MAXPOP
  error("If `popn > $(MAXPOP)` then modify code for indexing of time-lines!")
end ;
```

Note that (trivial) labelling issues arise if `popn > MAXPOP=20`.

We now set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(5inch, 3inch) ;

coordinates     = UnitBox(0, popn, duration, -popn, 
                  leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, 
                  bottompad=0.5inch, toppad=0.5inch) ;
```


# Basic image template elements
First we construct the time axis, with tick marks at integer times:
```{julia}
time_axis    = 
  (context(), 
   line([(0,0), (duration, 0)]), stroke("black"), linewidth(0.5mm)
  ) ;

tic          = -0.2cy
step         = 10^floor(Int, log10(duration))
tic_loc1     = [((x,0), (x, tic)) for x in 0:step:duration]
tic_loc2     = [((x,0), (x, tic)) for x in 0:0.5step:duration]
tic_loc3     = [((x,0), (x, 0.5tic)) for x in 0:0.1step:duration]

ticks1        =
 (context(), 
   line(tic_loc1), 
     stroke("black"), linewidth(0.2mm),
  ) ;

ticks2       =
 (context(), 
   line(tic_loc2), 
     stroke("black"), linewidth(0.1mm),
  ) ;

ticks3       =
 (context(), 
   line(tic_loc3), 
     stroke("black"), linewidth(0.1mm),
  ) ;

label_height = 0cy + 0.25inch
tick_labels  =
  (context(),
    text(0:duration, [label_height], ["$i" for i in 0:duration], 
      [hcenter], [vbottom]), 
    stroke("grey"), fontsize(7pt)
  ) ;
```


Now we build the time-lines, labelled by circled integers.
The definition of `circ_labels` needs to be changed if `popn > MAXPOP=20`,
as unicode then runs out of circled integers!
```{julia}
lab_xoffset  = 0cx - 0.25inch
circ_labels  = [string(Char(0x00002460+i-1)) for i in 1:popn]
line_labels  = (context(),
    text([lab_xoffset], [i for i in 1:popn], circ_labels,
      [hleft], [vcenter]), 
    stroke("grey"), fontsize(7pt)
  ) ;
lines        = (context(),
  line([[(0, k), (duration, k)] for k in 1:popn]), 
  stroke("black"), linewidth(0.5mm)
  ) ;
```

# Drawing the underlying scaffolding
@fig-scaffolding illustrates the underlying scaffolding for (almost) all our diagrams:
```{julia}
#| label: fig-scaffolding
#| fig-cap: "Scaffolding"
compose(context(units=coordinates), 
  (context(), rectangle(), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.3)),
  time_axis,
  ticks1, ticks2, ticks3,
  tick_labels,
  line_labels,
  lines
)
```

# An innovation for an unconditioned \(SIR\) epidemic
We introduce some content by considering potential incidents underlying
an unconditional epidemic.
```{julia}
I = epi.Infection
R = epi.Removal

env0 = epi.Innovation(5, 
  epi.AbstractInfection[
    I(0.5,2,5), I(0.7,1,2), I(0.8,1,2), I(0.9,2,4), I(1.15,3,4), I(1.2,2,3),
    I(1.3,1,2), I(1.4,4,5), I(1.41,1,4), I(1.5,2,4), I(1.9,3,5), I(1.8,3,4)
    ], 
  epi.Removal[
    R(0.6,5), R(1.1,1), R(1.25,5), R(1.6,2), R(1.7,2)
    ],
  epi.CRemoval[]
) ;
```

Then we must plot epidemics arising from the time-sequence of potential incidents:
```{julia}
epi.chronology(env0)
```

The required figure is @fig-potential.
```{julia}
#| label: fig-potential
#| fig-cap: "Potential incidents, including both removals and infections."

radius = 0.05

compose(context(units=coordinates), 
  (context(), rectangle(), fill("bisque"), fillopacity(0.1)),
  time_axis,
  ticks1, ticks2, ticks3,
  tick_labels,
  line_labels,
  lines,
  
  (context(), 
    circle([inc.t for inc in env0.removals], 
           [inc.target for inc in env0.removals],
           [radius]),
    fill("blue"), fillopacity(0.1), stroke("blue")
  ),
  
  (context(), 
    circle([inc.t for inc in env0.infections], 
           [inc.infector for inc in env0.infections],
           [radius]),
    fill("yellow"), fillopacity(0.1), stroke("orange")
  ),

  (context(units=coordinates), 
    line([[(inc.t, inc.infector+4radius), (inc.t, inc.infectee)]
           for inc in env0.infections]),
    line([[(inc.t-0.5radius, inc.infectee-0.125), 
           (inc.t, inc.infectee), 
           (inc.t+0.5radius, inc.infectee-0.125)]
           for inc in env0.infections]),
    stroke("orange")
  )
)
```

::: {.callout-caution}
Note the hard-wired way in which arrows are drawn in last chunk!.
:::
